preamble: Retroflexion and devoicing of the voiced alveolo-palatal fricative [ʑ] to [ʂ]. The documented case is the Middle Chinese 船 initial, reconstructed as [ʑ] (Baxter zy-) by Baxter, Zhengzhang and Pulleyblank, whose values for 船 and 禪 reverse the traditional rime-table assignment. By the rime-table (Late Middle Chinese) stage the palatal sibilants had already merged with the retroflex ones, and Pulleyblank gives the merged 船/禪 initial as breathy-voiced [ʂɦ]. In Standard Mandarin most 船 words are read with sh- [ʂ], as in 神 shén, 實 shí, 食 shí, 舌 shé and 述 shù; a few level-tone words instead have aspirated ch- (see zh_palatal_to_ch_retroflex_aspirated). Chengdu Sichuanese, which lacks retroflexes, has [s] in the same words.
sources: Baxter, William H. (1992). A Handbook of Old Chinese Phonology. Mouton de Gruyter. https://doi.org/10.1515/9783110857085
